content.content:
3933:model FreeMinecraftServer {
3934-  id             String               @id @default(cuid())
3935-  userId         String               @unique
3936-  user           User                 @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
3937-  // Public-facing name: reachable at `<subdomain>.<free_minecraft_domain>`.
3938-  // Validated against SUBDOMAIN_RE (lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts) at creation —
3939-  // lowercase alnum/hyphen, 3-20 chars — the same shape a DNS label allows.
3940-  subdomain      String               @unique
3941-  // The actual `docker run --name` on freemc-host; derived from `id` (not
3942-  // `subdomain`) so a container is never renamed if a future feature lets a
3943-  // player change their subdomain — the container identity and the public name
3944-  // are deliberately decoupled.
3945-  containerName  String               @unique
3946-  // CREATING: DB row exists, docker run hasn't been confirmed yet (worker job
3947-  // pending/running). READY: container exists on the host — mc-router owns
3948-  // whether it's actually awake or asleep at any given moment; we don't mirror
3949-  // that live state here to avoid it going stale. DELETING/DELETED: teardown
3950-  // requested/complete.
3951-  status         String               @default("CREATING")
3952-  // Cosmetic display name shown in the dashboard — defaults to the subdomain,
3953-  // distinct from it so renaming never touches the connect address or the
3954-  // container's mc-router label.
3955-  name           String?
3956-  // DEPRECATED — kept only for backward compatibility with the legacy
3957-  // dashboard UI (components/customer/freemc/*.tsx) that still reads a flat
3958-  // "preset" instead of the two-axis gameType/gameMode model below (that UI
3959-  // is being replaced in a parallel change; do not build anything new
3960-  // against this field). Mirrors activeGameType, EXCEPT when activeGameType
3961-  // is "vanilla" and activeGameMode isn't "survival" — then it mirrors
3962-  // activeGameMode instead (creative/hardcore/peaceful), matching the exact
3963-  // flat keys the old FREEMC_PRESETS map used, so legacy cards still
334:const PUBLIC_TOOL_NAMES = new Set(PUBLIC_TOOLS.map((t) => t.name));

I'm sketching out an eval harness: a JSON file of anonymized test cases with expected regex matches and word limits, plus a runner script that compares the new kbAnswer function (run anonymously with dry-run mode) against the old variant.

For the old variant, I need to pull the legacy lib/kb-llm.ts, kb-system.ts, kb-tools.ts, and kb.ts from main and rewrite their import paths to point at local legacy copies instead of the @/lib aliases, since those old files reference each other. Since both variants run as anonymous users, writes like opening support tickets stay unavailable, keeping the eval side-effect free, and I still need to check whether tsx resolves tsconfig path aliases for files placed under the legacy folder.

I'll need to load the production env vars (DB url, encryption key) locally so resolveBotKey's decrypt works, treating this as acceptable since it's for a dry-run using the platform's configured key rather than live customer writes. For scoring, I'm combining rule-based checks (must/must-not phrases, word limits, handoff expectations) with an LLM judge model that rates correctness, helpfulness, and tone using the same key, and I need to make sure handoff cases are matched by checking the result kind and that conversation history is passed in properly as sender rows.

With roughly 30 cases across two variants and several tool rounds, cost should stay manageable using the smaller judge model. I'm drafting the actual test cases from the audit now—covering pricing questions, free server setup instructions, Turkish-language prompts with specific required/forbidden phrase patterns, and language-capability checks requiring Turkish characters in replies.

Continuing through the remaining cases, I'm specifying expected patterns for region availability (Singapore servers), dedicated IP inclusion, CPU/vCPU dedication claims for Singapore VPS plans, and refund policy timing—each with precise must/mustNot regex checks to catch inaccurate or overpromising responses.

I'm also covering payment method questions (PayPal yes, GCash no), Windows VPS availability (should route to team rather than falsely confirm), and starting on the uptime SLA question.

Continuing through the remaining test cases: uptime SLA (99.9%, not 99.98 or 100%), ticket response time (one business day, not minutes), the Discord link, and handoff triggers for "operator," wanting a human, hacked accounts. I'm also adding checks for cheapest VPS pricing ($8.88) without handoff, and file-related questions about Valheim world uploads and downloading game server files.

Then I move through backup policy wording (should mention manual backups and the Backups tab, not claim automatic daily backups), server region change requests (should route to the team, not suggest self-service via Settings), Bedrock players joining the free Java-only server, and Project Zomboid 12GB pricing (confirming the $24 intro rate renews at $34.56).

I also need to verify the DDoS protection provider case avoids naming specific companies, handle a Korean refund question requiring Hangul script rather than Chinese characters, and check the port 80/dedicated IP question for VPS hosting. All responses should stay under 110 words, and I'm noting that signed-in account cases should be skipped since they'd expose real account data—sticking to anonymous scenarios is the safer approach. # Live-chat bot and ticket corpus audit (2026-10-06)

Source: the prod DB, SELECT only. Customer data is summarised here. Snippets are short and anonymised.

## Corpus

**Live chat:** 94 conversations, 1,032 messages.
- 495 visitor messages, 313 human-agent messages, 224 bot messages.
- 90 conversations had a bot message. 44 had a human agent.

**Bot messages by type:**

| Type | Count |
|---|---|
| Model (LLM) answers | 161 |
| Pre-rework keyword or retrieval era (14–15 Aug: blog-snippet dumps, canned clarifiers) | 16 |
| Canned "Let me get a teammate…" | 20 |
| "None of our team are free…" | 11 |
| "Transferred to a ticket" (admin action) | 8 |
| Degraded "brief problem reaching my assistant" (dead key, 25–26 Aug) | 5 |
| Empty body (the model emitted only a `[[cards]]` directive) | 3 |

**Tickets:** 77 tickets, about 850 messages.
- 439 from customers, 411 from staff.
- 11 of the staff messages are bot chat transcripts copied in with an `[AI reply]` prefix.
- **No AI-drafted or auto-sent ticket reply path exists in the code.** I checked every `askClaude` caller. The only AI write to Ticket is the chat tool `open_support_ticket`, which creates a NEW ticket owned by the customer. It is now consent-gated (see below).

**Reply length:**
- Bot model answers: median 66 words, p90 132, max 244. 92 of 161 were over 60 words and 45 were over 100.
- Human chat agents: median 11 words, p90 42.
- Human ticket replies: median 18 words, p90 147.

**Human requests:** customers asked "talk to a human" 26 times. The bot never spoke after an agent joined (0 violations), so the aiPaused and agent gate was already working.

## Classification of the 161 bot model answers

These are hand-labelled, and one answer can carry several labels.

| Label | Count |
|---|---|
| Correct and clean | 55 (34%) |
| Correct but too long or robotic | +11 |
| Wrong fact | 42 |
| Hallucinated feature, button, policy or promise | 24 |
| **Any factual error (wrong or hallucinated)** | **65 (40%)** |
| Too long (labelled) | 47 (45 are over 100 words) |
| Robotic or filler | 11 |
| Missing information | 6 |
| Should have escalated | 3 |
| Should NOT have opened a ticket or handed off without consent | 8 |
| Leaked internals | 2 |
| Empty body | 3 |

## Top failure patterns (anonymised)

1. **Stale or static facts contradicted the product.** This was the biggest category.
   - "We don't have a 4GB Valheim tier". It exists at $9.99. Seen 3 times.
   - "Project Zomboid pricing isn't in my info". It is in the catalogue.
   - "Nxeon doesn't offer per-region selection". Singapore, Canada and Germany are picked in the wizard.
   - "No free Minecraft… port-forward your home router". Seen 3 times, including in Turkish, before the KB fix.
   - "every VPS includes a dedicated IPv4". Reality: one is assigned only when the pool has a free address, otherwise shared NAT. The add-on costs $2.99. Singapore's pool currently has 0 free.
   - "I don't see a 30-day money-back guarantee". The bot argued with a customer who had seen the checkout. The real rule is a **72-hour** first-order guarantee.
   - "Windows Server 2016 or any OS you want". There is no Windows image.
   - Retired "Nano" VPS quoted.
2. **Invented UI and procedures.**
   - It walked a customer through "Settings tab → three-dot menu → Danger Zone → scroll down" for 6 turns looking for a cancel button.
   - It said "a temporary password gets emailed to you". Passwords are never emailed.
   - It described an "upload .mcaddon in the Add-ons section" that doesn't exist.
   - It said "the console/RCON lets you swap in a custom world".
   - It said "switching to Fabric wipes your world". It doesn't.
3. **Promises it couldn't keep.**
   - "They typically respond within the hour during business hours".
   - "it'll refund the charge since it failed to provision". Failed provisions are not auto-refunded.
   - "the team will restart that VM for you".
   - "I've noted your email and someone will reach out". No mechanism exists.
   - "let me search that… give me a sec?"
   - "refund processes on the next billing cycle".
4. **Wrong language.**
   - A Korean question was answered in Chinese.
   - Japanese questions were treated as off-topic and answered in English.
   - "I'm only set up to chat in English". This was false, and the same bot answered in Arabic and Turkish elsewhere.
5. **Tickets opened without asking.** 7 of 15 bot tickets were opened on a first message or a quick-reply chip ("I need technical help…"), worded as if the customer wrote them. Raw ids like `[cm…]` were shown to customers.
6. **Too long, and robotic in places.** Examples: 244-word refund replies, a 239-word game list, "(Results got cut off, but you've got the idea…)", and "the knowledge base says do not quote a region…", which leaked the instructions.
7. **The tool didn't show free Minecraft servers.** Free-tier owners were told "you don't have any active services" 4 times. The table is separate.
8. **Bad handoff loop.**
   - A repeat "talk to a human" produced wait, then "none free… drop your email for a callback" (when the email was already known), then the same again. This happened 3 times in one chat.
   - "operator" was answered as Minecraft `/op`.
   - The handoff regex also fired on "someone", "agent", "rep" and "live chat" inside normal questions.

**Human-agent issues for the owner** (not changed by this branch):
- The OVH vendor name was used in one chat reply.
- "Our provider's stated policy" and "the maintenance they are performing" appeared in tickets.
- Agents gave "CPU is dedicated" and "99.99% / 99.80%" uptime figures with no backing in the code. Standard VPS CPU is shared and oversubscribed. /legal/sla says 99.9%.
- A competitor was disparaged.
- A root password was posted in plain text in a ticket.
- A stock Trustpilot closer was sent 7 times, sometimes badly timed.

## What worked (human exemplars → style rules)

- **Answer first, outcome first.** For example: "We've sorted this at the network layer — you're now on a dedicated address", followed by the connection details.
- **Short, specific pings for status.** For example: "What address are you connecting to? We'll check the logs."
- **Honest limits stated plainly**, with a real alternative. For example: "no extract button yet — upload the zip and we'll extract it for you".
- **Ask one targeted question** (player count, game, location) before sizing.
- **Explicit permission before a risky step**, and data integrity stated first.

## What customers actually ask (chat plus tickets, by frequency)

1. Server down, won't start, stuck provisioning or ERROR. "The VM must be running…" alone appeared 4 times.
2. Game config, mods, plugins, world upload or download, file manager.
3. Ports, IP, dedicated IPv4, NAT, port 80/443. There were 4 near-identical tickets.
4. Prices and tiers per game, intro vs renewal ("will it go up after month one?").
5. Region and latency: move to Singapore from Germany or Canada.
6. Refunds and the money-back guarantee, cancellation, wallet refund.
7. CPU model, dedicated vs shared vCPU, steal.
8. Free Minecraft (where it is, Bedrock?).
9. DDoS capacity and vendor.
10. Windows, custom specs, custom quotes.
11. Payment methods (GCash, PayPal), wallet top-up amounts.
12. Support and Discord link, response time, SLA.
13. Root password, login and email change.

# Ground truth used by the chat assistant (verified 2026-10-06, code plus prod SELECT)

The live versions of these facts are served by `get_platform_facts` (lib/kb-facts.ts). This page is a snapshot.

## Regions and network

**Regions** (lib/node-regions.ts, Node table):
- Singapore (sgp1: 4 nodes, 2 accepting new orders), Canada (bhs1) and Germany (fsn1).
- The location is picked in the deploy wizard. A full region refuses the order and suggests others (lib/region-placement.ts).
- Shared hosting has no location choice.
- Free Minecraft is on node-2, which is Germany.
- Region moves are not self-serve. `region_transfer_enabled` is off, so moves are done by the team.

**IPv4:**
- VPS: `dedicated_ip_default=true`. A VPS gets a dedicated IP only when the region's pool has a FREE address, otherwise it uses shared NAT (worker/index.ts:825-856).
- Pool right now: Singapore 0 free, Germany 1 free, Canada 1 free.
- Add-on price is $2.99/mo (Setting `dedicated_ip_price_cents=299`). It can be bought at checkout or later, for VPS and game servers.
- NAT port forwards: up to 10 per server, public ports 20000-29999 (lib/actions-server.ts:252, lib/ipam.ts).

**CPU:**
- No CPU model is stored. No pinning is implemented. vCPU is oversubscribed, RAM ×1.5 and disk ×3 (lib/capacity.ts).
- **Marketing pages claim "dedicated vCPU" and "AMD EPYC 9654" / "AMD Ryzen", which the code doesn't back.** This needs an owner decision.

**DDoS:**
- "Always-on" in marketing. The homepage claims "up to 1 Tbps".
- The bot quotes no number and no vendor.

## OS images, root password, setup time

**OS images:** Ubuntu 20.04/22.04/24.04, Debian 11/12/13, AlmaLinux 8/9 and Rocky 8/9, plus panels and apps. There is no Windows image and no custom ISO.

**Root password:**
- Click-to-reveal in the Root access card, with a reset button (`resetRootPassword`).
- It is never emailed (lib/email-templates.ts).

**Setup time:**
- The provisioning overlay says "usually under two minutes".
- The "47 seconds" brand tagline is left alone.

## Money

**Refunds** (lib/refund-policy.ts):
- 72-hour first-order money-back. It is processed manually by an admin; nothing auto-refunds it.
- Immediate VPS cancel credits the unused term to the WALLET.
- Game servers get $0 on immediate cancel (proration.ts:279).
- Hosting cancel gets no refund.
- Domains are non-refundable.
- Wallet-to-card refunds are discretionary (terms.ts:54).

**Payments:**
- Card via Stripe, plus Apple Pay and Google Pay through the Stripe express element.
- PayPal is live: env configured, kill switch defaults on.
- Crypto: not configured.
- Local methods (PayNow etc.): all off.
- No GCash and no bank transfer.
- Everything is charged in USD.
- Wallet top-up: preset or custom amount, $5 to $5000.

**Terms and dunning:**
- Terms: annual −20%, 24 months −30%, 36 months −40%. Domains: 2 years −5%, 3 years −10%.
- Intro price applies to the whole first term (`introTermMonths` is NULL).
- Dunning: retries on days 1, 3 and 5, then suspension. With no card, suspension comes after 3 days. Warning on day 7, deletion on day 14.

**Coupons:**
- WELCOME10 (the bot coupon) is valid: 10%, first order, 200 uses, expires 2027-08.
- TRIAL798 (the 7-day trial) expired 2026-09-29, so there is no trial now.
- First month free is HOSTING only.

**Expired coupons still flagged active=true:** NXSAVE40, NXFLASH40, WINTER50, PEERPUSH20, FREEMONTH and TRIAL798. They are harmless if expiry is enforced, but worth a cleanup.

## Support and SLA

- Support promise: "A human replies to every message within one business day" (lib/support-promise.ts). The game-servers marketing page says "24/7 Expert Support", which contradicts it. **Owner decision needed.**
- SLA (/legal/sla): a 99.9% target with 10/25/50% wallet credits. The PromoCarousel shows "99.98%". **Owner decision needed.**
- Discord: https://discord.gg/hqVZdDJH2 (PromoCarousel).
- No legal entity, country or registration number is published. A human agent told a customer "Canada".

## Game panel

**Tabs:** Overview, Console, Files, Mods & Plugins, Backups, Players, Schedules, Settings, Activity. There is no Manage tab and no Networking tab.

**IPv4:**
- VPS: `dedicated_ip_default=true`. A VPS gets a dedicated IP only when the region's pool has a FREE address, otherwise it uses shared NAT (worker/index.ts:825-856).
- Pool right now: Singapore 0 free, Germany 1 free, Canada 1 free.
- Add-on price is $2.99/mo (Setting `dedicated_ip_price_cents=299`). It can be bought at checkout or later, for VPS and game servers.

## Live-chat AI responder rework (2026-10-06, branch `feature/ai-responses-rework`)

**Why.** I audited every live-chat conversation (94 conversations, 161 model answers) and every ticket (77). The full report is in `/root/agent-notes/ai-responses/AUDIT.md`. Key findings:
- 40% of the bot's answers had a factual error or a hallucination. The main errors:
  - "every VPS has a dedicated IP"
  - "we don't do regions"
  - "no 4 GB Valheim"
  - "no free Minecraft"
  - it denied the money-back guarantee
- It invented buttons and procedures, and promised reply times and refunds.
- It answered in the wrong language.
- It opened tickets without asking.
- Its replies were 5× longer than the human team's (bot median 66 words, humans 11).

**What changed** (AI responder logic only; chat UI, transport and realtime are untouched):
- **`lib/kb-facts.ts`: new `get_platform_facts` tool.** It reads live facts at answer time from the same code, settings and tables the product uses:
  - regions (Node)
  - NAT, port forwards and dedicated-IP price and pool
  - refunds (`lib/refund-policy.ts`)
  - payment methods (PayPal and crypto config, local-method flags)
  - billing terms and dunning (`dunningConfig`)
  - support promise and SLA
  - OS images (OsTemplate)
  - add-on prices
  - hardware honesty (no CPU model, no dedicated cores)
  - game-panel features
  - the free Minecraft tier
- **`lib/kb-style.ts`: pure format guard.** It flags each of the following:
  - empty replies
  - soft limit of 90 words, hard limit of 140
  - more than 5 list items
  - more than 2 links
  - filler openers, sign-offs, canned closers
  - "only English" and "as an AI"
  - internal leaks (knowledge base, tool names, directives)
  - **any infrastructure vendor name or "provider"**
  - an invented SLA or response time (only the published 99.9% target and "one business day" are allowed)
  - raw cuids, impossible follow-up promises, over-apology, and non-nxeon.cloud links

  `lib/kb-llm.ts` `finalizeReply()` runs tidy, check, ONE rewrite call when a serious rule breaks, a sentence drop for any remaining hard violation, and a hard clamp.
- **`lib/kb-escalation.ts`:**
  - `humanIntent` now matches explicit asks only, in several languages. "can someone tell me the price" no longer stops the bot. A bare "operator" does hand off.
  - `riskCategory` sends account security, chargebacks/disputes and legal/abuse straight to a human.
  - `ticketConsent` gates ticket opening.
- **`lib/kb-tools.ts`:**
  - Adds `get_platform_facts` and `hand_off_to_human`, so the model can escalate itself in any language.
  - `open_support_ticket` is refused unless the customer asked for a ticket, or said yes to the bot's offer. The ticket body is labelled "[Opened from live chat by the Nxeon assistant, with the customer's OK]".
  - `list_services` and the overview now include the free Minecraft server (a separate table, so before this the bot told owners "no services").
  - `runChatTool(…, ctx)` takes `{ currentMessage, previousBotMessage, dryRun }`. dryRun stubs every write.
- **`lib/kb-llm.ts` prompt:**
  - A short, rule-first system prompt: answer first, 1–3 sentences, the customer's language, one question at most, no filler.
  - Hard fact rules: tools or the KB only, no invented UI, no promises, no vendor names. Clear handoff rules.
  - Teammate messages in history are marked `[Nxeon teammate]` and must never be contradicted.
  - The admin `kb_bot_coupon` is only offered if the Coupon row is really redeemable.
  - `lib/anthropic.ts` `askClaudeWithTools({ keepInterimText })` is opt-in. It keeps answer text the model wrote before a tool call. That text was being lost, so handoffs arrived without the answer.
- **`lib/kb-system.ts` / `kb-faq.ts` / `kb-catalog.ts`:** the KB was rewritten against the code. Corrected:
  - dedicated IP
  - regions
  - OS list
  - 72-hour refund processed by the team
  - PayPal
  - "one business day"
  - the SLA's 99.9% target
  - Discord link
  - game panel (no "Manage" tab; automatic backups are OFF by default; slots are not a cap)
  - free MC (Java only, own panel)
  - VPS cards no longer say "Dedicated IPv4"
- **`lib/kb-run.ts`:**
  - The model-written handoff line (in the customer's language) replaces the canned one.
  - A repeated "talk to a human" within 30 minutes of "nobody's free" gets one short reminder instead of the wait/no-agent loop and another email.
  - The canned lines no longer promise a "callback" or ask for an email we already have.
  - The degraded reply now emails the on-duty address, so its "the team has your message" is true.
  - The `aiPaused` / agent-replied / assigned gates are unchanged: the bot stays silent once a human is in.

**Ticket replies.** There is no AI-drafted or auto-sent ticket reply anywhere in the code. I verified every `askClaude` caller. Staff ticket replies stay human-only. The only AI write to a ticket is creating a new, consented ticket from chat.

**Eval.** `scripts/ai-eval/run.ts` (with `cases.json`) has 35 anonymised real questions. Each case has must / mustNot regexes, an expected handoff, the format check, and a Haiku judge.
- It runs as an anonymous visitor, in dry run, and never calls `runAssistant`. It writes nothing to the DB.
- `--variant old --ref main` extracts the old responder from git into `.legacy/` (gitignored) for a before/after comparison.
- Run: `set -a; . /opt/nxeon/.env; set +a; npx tsx scripts/ai-eval/run.ts --variant new`.

**Tests.** `test/kb-style-escalation.test.ts` covers the following, all pure:
- the format guard and the tidy/clamp/drop helpers
- human intent (positive and negative)
- risk categories
- ticket consent
- the router refusing an unconsented ticket, and dry-run
- the tool set
- KB regressions
- history marking
EOF
git add docs/DOCUMENTATION.md && git commit -q -m "Docs: live-chat AI responder rework

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && git log --oneline -1

input.message:
The AI responder rework is committed on `feature/ai-responses-rework` (worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-aibot`, head `2957bcf405`, 5 commits). It's not merged or deployed, and nothing was sent to any customer, ticket, chat, Discord or email. One urgent thing first: the platform's Anthropic key ran out of credit during my eval runs ("credit balance is too low"). The live chat bot uses that same key, so in prod it is probably answering every message with the fallback "I can't pull up an answer right now" line. The owner needs to add credit or swap the key (admin → Settings → AI assistant → Test connection).

`npx tsc --noEmit` is clean. On the full suite I got 43 failures against the 46 baseline, and none of them are new. The 3 "fixed" ones are the uid-state tests, probably environment-related. My changes stay in the responder logic; no chat UI, transport or realtime files were touched.

**AI ticket replies:** none exist anywhere in the code (I checked every place the code calls Claude), so nothing can auto-send to a ticket. The only AI write is the chat tool that opens a new ticket. That tool is now refused unless the customer asked for a ticket or said yes to the bot's offer, and the ticket is labelled as opened by the assistant.

**Audit** (`/root/agent-notes/ai-responses/AUDIT.md`):
- **Corpus:** 94 chats (1,032 messages, 161 model answers) and 77 tickets (about 850 messages).
- **Accuracy:** 40% of the bot's answers (65 of 161) had a wrong or invented fact. Only 34% were correct and clean.
- **Length:** the bot's median reply was 66 words (p90 132); the human agents' median was 11.
- **Top patterns:**
  1. Facts that had drifted from the product:
     - "every VPS includes a dedicated IP" (it falls back to a shared IP when the pool is empty; Singapore has 0 free now)
     - "no region choice" (Singapore, Canada and Germany are all selectable)
     - "no 4 GB Valheim" (it exists at $9.99)
     - "no free Minecraft, port-forward your router"
     - "no 30-day guarantee" (the real rule is 72 hours)
     - Windows "or any OS"
  2. Made-up buttons and steps ("Danger Zone", "temporary password emailed").
  3. Promises it couldn't keep ("within the hour", "it'll refund", "give me a sec").
  4. Wrong language: a Korean question answered in Chinese, and "I only speak English".
  5. 7 of 15 bot tickets opened without asking.
  6. Leaks such as "the knowledge base says…" and "results got cut off", plus 3 empty replies.
  7. Free Minecraft servers were invisible to the account tool, so owners were told they had no services.
  8. A repeat "talk to a human" looped back to "drop your email for a callback".
- **Most-asked topics:** server down or stuck, game mods/files/worlds, IPs and ports, prices and renewals, moving to Singapore, refunds, CPU model and dedicated cores, free Minecraft, DDoS, Windows or custom specs, payment methods.

**What changed:**
- **Live facts tool** (`lib/kb-facts.ts`): the bot now reads regions, shared IP vs dedicated IP and the $2.99 add-on, refunds, payment methods (PayPal is live), billing and failed-payment rules, the support promise and SLA, OS images, add-on prices, CPU honesty, game-panel features and the free tier from the live code, settings and database when it answers.
- **Reply guard** (`lib/kb-style.ts`): checks length (90 words soft, 140 hard), filler, sign-offs, internal leaks, any vendor or "provider" mention, invented SLAs, raw ids, impossible promises and wrong domains. A failing draft gets one rewrite, then any bad sentence is dropped and the reply is cut to length.
- **Escalation** (`lib/kb-escalation.ts`): only explicit asks for a person count, in several languages; account security, chargebacks and legal threats go straight to a human; ticket opening needs consent. The model also gets a `hand_off_to_human` tool.
